message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me not to attend my great aunt's funeral. Let me break this down step by step. First, I just found out about her passing. My mom told me, and I was really confused because I've never heard of her before. The only time I met her was when I was a baby, like 1 or 2 years old. I don't remember anything about her, and she's never been mentioned in our family conversations. So, to me, she's practically a stranger. My mom is insisting I go to the funeral. She says it's out of respect and to support her. But I'm really awkward at funerals, especially for people I don't know well. I mean, I've been to a few funerals for people I know, but this is different. I don't even know who this person is beyond a name. How can I respect someone I don't know or remember? She also mentioned that this is a chance to meet a larger branch of the family. There might be hundreds of people there, but I've only seen about 10 of them more than once. It feels like I'm gate-crashing their family event. I don't know anyone, and I don't think they'd want me there either. It's not like I have a close relationship with them. I'm also thinking about the effort it would take to attend. I'm still in college, and this is a big commitment. I don't know if it's worth it for someone I don't even know. Plus, I'm not sure how to behave in such a situation. I don't want to make things worse by being there and not knowing what to do. My mom tried to guilt-trip me, which made me feel bad, but I still don't see the point. I don't think attending the funeral would bring me any closure or help me in any way. It's more of an obligation that doesn't feel meaningful to me. So, considering all this, I don't feel morally obligated to attend. My presence wouldn't mean much, and it's not something I'm comfortable with. I think it's okay to prioritize my own feelings and circumstances in this situation.
